paragraphs.title: David Searches for a Descendant of Saul

answers: Someone remaining from the house of Saul
easy.explanation: David asked whether anyone remained of Saul's house.
easy.q: Whom did David seek to find?

easy.explanation: David wanted to show kindness for Jonathan's sake.
easy.q: For whose sake did David want to show kindness?

easy.explanation: Ziba told David about Jonathan's son.

answers: He was lame on his feet
He was a servant in Saul's house
medium.explanation: Ziba said that Jonathan's son was lame on his feet.
medium.q: What condition did Ziba say Mephibosheth had?

answers: He sent Ziba to till the land
medium.explanation: David sent and fetched Mephibosheth from Machir's house.
medium.q: What did David do after learning where Mephibosheth was?

answers: In the house of Machir at Lo-debar
medium.explanation: Ziba said Mephibosheth was in Machir's house in Lo-debar.

answers: He wanted to honor his covenant relationship with Jonathan
He wanted to punish Saul's household
challenge.explanation: David twice connects his kindness with Jonathan.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David's repeated desire to show kindness?

challenge.explanation: Ziba identifies Mephibosheth as Jonathan's son.
challenge.q: Which detail connects Mephibosheth to Saul's family through Jonathan?

answers: David fetches Mephibosheth, then asks about Saul's house
Ziba tells David about Mephibosheth, David sends for him, and Mephibosheth is brought to David
Machir brings Ziba, and David sends for Machir
challenge.explanation: Ziba gives the information, David sends for Mephibosheth, and Mephibosheth is brought from Machir's house.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

answers: He fell on his face and showed reverence
He sat on the king's throne
easy.explanation: Mephibosheth fell on his face and did reverence before David.
easy.q: What did Mephibosheth do when he came to David?
What did David tell Mephibosheth not to do?

easy.explanation: David promised that Mephibosheth would eat bread continually at his table.
easy.q: Where did David promise that Mephibosheth would continually eat?

answers: To restore Saul's land to him and have him eat at the king's table
To send him back to Machir's house
medium.explanation: David promised to restore Saul's land and provide him a place at the king's table.
medium.q: What kindness did David promise to show Mephibosheth?

medium.explanation: Mephibosheth humbled himself and called himself a dead dog.
medium.q: How did Mephibosheth respond to David's words?

medium.explanation: David promised Mephibosheth a gracious favor because of Jonathan.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “kindness” most nearly mean?

answers: He considered himself unworthy of honor
challenge.explanation: Calling himself a dead dog expresses deep humility and lowliness.
challenge.q: What does Mephibosheth's response reveal about how he viewed himself before David?

answers: Mephibosheth had come before the king and bowed in fear
Mephibosheth was working in the fields
Mephibosheth was already eating at the king's table
challenge.explanation: Mephibosheth's fearful approach before the king explains David's reassurance.
challenge.q: Why were David's words, “Fear not,” appropriate in this situation?

answers: He moves from living with Machir to receiving land and a place at the king's table
He moves from being king to being a servant
He moves from Jerusalem to Machir's house
challenge.explanation: David promises him Saul's land and continual access to the royal table.
challenge.q: What change in Mephibosheth's status begins with David's promise?

paragraphs.title: Restoration of Property and Management of the Land

easy.explanation: David gave it to Mephibosheth, Saul's master's son.
easy.q: To whom did David give all that belonged to Saul and his house?

answers: Ziba, his sons, and his servants
easy.explanation: Ziba, his sons, and his servants were assigned to till the land.
easy.q: Who was to till the land?

answers: As one of the king's sons
easy.explanation: Ziba said Mephibosheth would eat as one of the king's sons.
easy.q: How was Mephibosheth to eat at the king's table?

answers: Ziba and his household would till the land and bring in its produce so Mephibosheth would have food
Ziba would keep all the produce for himself
Mephibosheth would work in the fields instead of Ziba
medium.explanation: Ziba's household was to bring in the fruits so Mephibosheth would have food.
medium.q: What was the connection between Ziba's work and Mephibosheth's food?

medium.explanation: David instructed Ziba to work the land for Mephibosheth.
medium.q: What was Ziba instructed to do?

answers: That Mephibosheth received an honored place at the king's table
That he worked in the king's fields
That he served the king's sons
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Mephibosheth's honored status in the royal household.
medium.q: What does the phrase “as one of the king's sons” communicate?

answers: He restored Saul's property and provided continual food at his table
He gave him only work in the fields
He gave him only a place to live
challenge.explanation: David gave Mephibosheth both family property and a permanent place at the royal table.
challenge.q: How did David combine restoration of rights with daily care for Mephibosheth?

answers: The responsibility for the land involved an entire household, not just one man
Ziba had lost all his people
Ziba's sons became sons of the king
challenge.explanation: The passage lists Ziba, his sons, and his servants as those who would work the land.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the mention of Ziba's sons and servants?

answers: David grants Mephibosheth honor and rights and arranges how those promises will be fulfilled
David cancels his promise to Mephibosheth
David transfers all of Mephibosheth's rights to Ziba
challenge.explanation: The instructions to Ziba make David's promise practical and ongoing.
challenge.q: What idea connects David's words to Mephibosheth with his instructions to Ziba?

easy.explanation: The passage says that Mephibosheth had a son named Micha.
easy.q: What was the name of Mephibosheth's son?

answers: He was lame on both his feet
He was wounded in his hands
easy.explanation: The passage states that he was lame on both his feet.
easy.q: What was Mephibosheth's condition in his feet?

answers: They became sons of the king
medium.explanation: All who dwelt in Ziba's house became servants to Mephibosheth.
medium.q: What happened to the people who dwelt in Ziba's house?

answers: So that he could continually eat at the king's table
So that he could till Saul's land
So that he could live in Machir's house
medium.explanation: The verse connects his dwelling in Jerusalem with eating continually at the king's table.
medium.q: Why did Mephibosheth dwell in Jerusalem?

answers: Disabled or unable to walk normally
medium.explanation: The passage explains that Mephibosheth was lame on both feet.
medium.q: What does “lame” mean in this passage?

answers: He became a continual participant in the royal household
He was sent to work in the fields
challenge.explanation: Living in Jerusalem and eating continually at the king's table express his new royal status.
challenge.q: What does the connection between Mephibosheth's dwelling in Jerusalem and eating at the king's table show?

answers: Mephibosheth held an honored position although he was lame in both feet
Ziba was king although he was a servant
Micha worked in the fields although he was king
challenge.explanation: The passage presents both Mephibosheth's honored status and his physical disability.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized at the end of the chapter?

answers: His son Micha is named, and Ziba's household becomes his servants
He becomes an only son in Machir's house
He gives his property back to Saul's house
challenge.explanation: The passage names Micha and describes the servants belonging to Mephibosheth.
challenge.q: How is the continuation of Mephibosheth's family shown?
